header.title: iOS vs Windows parity divergences (machine-readable twin of PARITY_MAP.md)
header.format: Top level was a bare list of 216 records until the Phase 1 map (2026-11-15); since 2026-11-16 it is {header, items}. Record fields are unchanged; optional fields added over time: decision, queueNote, closedReason, crossReference, rebaseline (2026-11-16). Final pass 2026-11-18 (schemaVersion 3): status now holds the FINAL outcome (fixed, fixed-ui-unverified, blocked-needs-decision, wont-fix, cannot-reproduce, no-longer-divergent); statusBefore keeps the earlier value (open, decided or closed); statusWhere (files) and statusNote (what was done, or why not) come from the final result and statusCluster is the internal label of the work package that did the item (kept for traceability); dispositionPhase1 is set only where disposition changed (the 8 blocked-needs-decision items, planned as fix); openQuestions lists the needs-my-decision entries that name the item (kind formal or candidate). The windows.* and ios.* fields of an item describe the two sides AS MAPPED (the iOS side before the fix); the outcome is statusNote/statusWhere. Update 2026-11-19 (schemaVersion stays 3: only optional fields were added, nothing was removed or renamed): on the 23 items decided that day decisionUpdate ({date, outcome, text, codeChange}; outcome keep-ios, port or deviate-from-windows), statusBeforeDecision, decisionTests, decisionTestGap and, on the 4 code changes, codeChangeDetail; the 8 former blocked-needs-decision items also got dispositionBeforeDecision and closedReason (their disposition and status are wont-fix now); possibleWindowsDefect ({where: [file:line], what, scenario, severity, confidence} plus subItem, evidence, suggestedWindowsFix, whereNotes, group) and furtherPossibleWindowsDefects on the items where the research found a Windows problem (12 of the 23 decided items and EXP-17, EXP-M02, LP-22, COND-PLACE-01); openQuestions entries carry state (decided, partly-decided or open), decidedOn, outcome and resolution, and COND-PLACE-01 got its two open notes. The DBP-33 decision text was corrected (decision.userNote, decision.userNoteOriginal, queueNote). Header: decisions2026_11_19 (index of the decisions), counts, needsMyDecision (now the still-open index) and finalOutcome were rewritten.

notes: GENERAL RULE (user, 2026-11-16): If a Windows behavior looks accidental, internally inconsistent or unsafe, do NOT port it: it goes into the report's 'needs my decision' list with the Windows file:line and what was done meanwhile (keep the current iOS behavior).

Dispositions: fix = the Windows behavior is the spec and the item was ported (final status fixed or fixed-ui-unverified); wont-fix = closed by a user decision (closedReason says why); no-longer-divergent = the difference disappeared (iOS already fixed or Windows changed); cannot-reproduce = not reproducible on iOS; needs-decision = iOS behavior kept and listed for the user (final status blocked-needs-decision; the Phase 1 disposition is in dispositionPhase1); no item has this disposition since 2026-11-19: the user decided the 8 items (keep iOS, no code change), so their disposition and status are wont-fix and dispositionBeforeDecision records needs-decision. The 44 map questions were all answered 2026-11-16; the 8 formal items were NEW questions found while fixing, raised under the general rule above and decided on 2026-11-19.

Statuses (final, 2026-11-19; first set 2026-11-18): fixed = ported and covered by host unit tests and/or the Obj-C syntax check; fixed-ui-unverified = ported, but part of the behavior is Obj-C/UIKit/Metal/WebKit that was syntax-checked against hand-written stubs and, since the first successful CI run (2026-11-20 UTC), also compiles against the real iPhoneOS 18.5 SDK without errors, but has not run on a device or simulator and needs that check (statusNote names it); blocked-needs-decision = iOS behavior kept and the question listed for the user (no item has this status since 2026-11-19: the 8 items were decided and are wont-fix, statusBeforeDecision records it); wont-fix = closed by a user decision; cannot-reproduce; no-longer-divergent. statusBefore = the status before the final pass (open = not worked on, decided = a user decision is recorded, closed = nothing to do).

Decisions: 33 ids were answered "port" (31 became fix items, all of them applied or partly applied as shown by status; GEO-15 and EXP-17 chose option a and became wont-fix for winding and vertex-order parity, with the cross-reference to GEO-14) and 11 "keep" (wont-fix). MSH-16, EXP-22 and MSH-19b follow the FIXED Windows behavior (the re-baselined windows.behavior). Result for the 44 after the decisions of 2026-11-19: 24 fixed, 5 fixed-ui-unverified, 0 blocked-needs-decision, 15 wont-fix (on 2026-11-18 it was 25, 4, 2 and 13: IMP-20 and LP-24 became wont-fix and COND-STYLE-02 became fixed-ui-unverified on 2026-11-19).

RPV-22 is wont-fix for curved placement and the centre handle; its two remaining obligations are recorded in the notes of GEO-18 (draw existing curves) and RPV-M03 (drag must not corrupt the control point), which are fixed.

MSH-19b: final disposition fix (user decision) although the re-baseline found the plain-wall behavior already in iOS; the warning log with the takeoff UID, the empty-face union check and the catch of a throw (shared with RB-04) are done (status fixed).
iOS frame for expected values: iOS meshes are Y-up with (X, Z) = (-x_ost, -y_ost) (Core/Meshing/TakeoffMeshBuilder.hpp:8-9); the Windows test helpers use an identity frame (X = ost x).

The ios.where / ios.behavior fields and the iOS locations of the feature table in PARITY_MAP.md describe the code as mapped. Several iOS files were rewritten by the fixes (for example Services/ExportService.mm, Services/ProjectService.mm, PlanView/PlanView.mm); use statusWhere for the current location of the work.

DECISIONS OF 2026-11-19 (user message "Close out the open porting blockers"): 21 keep-iOS decisions without a code change (19 items; IMP-20 has three sub-rules, RPV-27 (a) and (b) are one record, DBP-04 covers DBP-05, SNP-01, LP-19 and LOAD-01) and 4 code changes written test-first (COND-STYLE-02 and COND-ELEV-01 deliberately deviate from the literal Windows behavior, DLG-FINITE-01 only for the whitespace-only Rise / Run half, UND-09). The 8 formal items DBP-04, BRW-09, EXP-12, EXP-13, EXP-16, IMP-20, LP-24 and RPV-29 changed from blocked-needs-decision to wont-fix; the candidate items keep their status (COND-STYLE-02 and COND-ELEV-01 moved from fixed to fixed-ui-unverified because their Obj-C part was then only syntax-checked; since 2026-11-20 UTC it also compiles against the real iOS SDK on CI, see finalOutcome.verification.ci). Index: header.decisions2026_11_19. What the user did not decide stays open: header.needsMyDecision.open.

POSSIBLE WINDOWS DEFECTS (2026-11-19): for every kept item that looks like a Windows defect the record has possibleWindowsDefect with the verified Windows file:line (18 defects on 16 items, counted per defect). They are suggestions for the Windows side and not ported; the Windows repo was only read.

VERIFICATION WORDING (2026-11-20 UTC): the statusNote, decisionTestGap and codeChangeDetail texts that say only syntax-checked against hand-written stubs are as of 2026-11-18/19 and are not rewritten one by one. The GitHub Actions workflow Build IPA has since run through every step on this code (finalOutcome.verification.ci): every Obj-C and Obj-C++ file compiles against the real iPhoneOS 18.5 SDK. Nothing has run on a device or simulator, so the 25 fixed-ui-unverified items still need that check (finalOutcome.notVerified).

keptNotADefect.subItem: NULL / missing TakeoffIncrements loads as 1.0 (already ported)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect.

keptNotADefect.subItem: restore from Deleted Bids with a vanished OrigBidProjectUID fails the whole restore group
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: a deliberate referential-integrity rule.

keptNotADefect.subItem: NameFontColor default (iOS writes 0 on insert)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect.

keptNotADefect.subItem: export error text 'Export function returned False'
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: deliberate and test-pinned wording.

keptNotADefect.subItem: page order = click order in multi-page exports
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: a harmless design choice.

keptNotADefect.subItem: (2) BidTexts.Name and BidCallOuts.Name encoded as latin-1 bytes, raising for characters outside latin-1 (iOS stores UTF-8 text)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect (on the import side): the legacy column is a latin-1 byte blob and Windows deliberately raises instead of silently replacing characters; decoding latin-1 never fails, so an OST/OSP produced by Windows always re-encodes.

keptNotADefect.subItem: (3) memo and IMAGE (longbinary) text stored as a UTF-8 BLOB (iOS keeps TEXT)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: deliberate and consistent.

keptNotADefect.subItem: cdn_type_name sentinel 'Unknown' in the loader (iOS keeps '')
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: 'Unknown' for no type and for a dangling type uid is a deliberate loader convention, mirrored by the entity default and several consumers; the dialog hides it (uid lookup first, so a real type named 'Unknown' still works).

keptNotADefect.subItem: is_top / z_value taken from the dialog but memory comes from a reload
keptNotADefect.why: Nothing of consequence: the two DTO keys are never persisted and Windows reloads the conditions from the database after every save, so Windows memory always equals what a reload derives from the name.

keptNotADefect.subItem: Normal flip in the 3D lighting (iOS flips towards the viewer, Windows orients normals to +z)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect on its own: orienting shading normals to +z is deliberate and test-pinned, and the shader lights with the raw normal on purpose.

keptNotADefect.subItem: Minimum interactive sizes (8 px count item / 2 px linear band at Windows view_scale 3.0; iOS uses 8/3 pt and 2/3 pt)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a Windows defect: the minimums are fixed pixel constants in scene pixels and are consistent in the renderer and the drag/placement code.

keptNotADefect.subItem: (a) negative marker anchor of an area with backouts (Qt subtracted-path point order versus iOS region centroid)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: Windows feeds the points of the Qt-subtracted path (several subpaths concatenated) into one polygon centroid, which is not the area centroid of the visible fill, but the contract (anchor inside the visible fill, with an interior fallback) is test-pinned and met.

keptNotADefect.subItem: Page switch also clears the selected / place condition and the FAB placement availability on iOS (Windows keeps the sidebar condition highlighted)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: Windows drops the takeoff selection on a page switch (pinned) and leaves the sidebar condition highlighted; iOS clearing the condition as well is the safe direction.

keptNotADefect.subItem: insert_takeoffs validates every parent against rows that exist BEFORE the batch (iOS accepts a parent restored earlier in the same batch)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a Windows defect: Windows never restores a takeoff under its original uid (the writer allocates new uids), so a parent has to exist before the insert.

keptNotADefect.subItem: drag validity (polygon_is_valid) evaluated on scene coordinates instead of OST coordinates
keptNotADefect.why: Not a practical defect: validity is decided on coordinates scaled by OST * 72 * view_scale / scale_ratio, so for exactly collinear or touching (degenerate) polygons the answer can depend on floating-point rounding of that scale factor.

keptNotADefect.subItem: HTML export includes hidden-layer conditions (iOS filters them)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: deliberate and test-pinned.

keptNotADefect.subItem: export page and takeoff order follows the user's selection order (iOS sorts)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: deliberate and pinned.

keptNotADefect.subItem: LZX and Quantum cabinet compression (iOS decodes stored and MSZIP only)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a Windows problem.

keptNotADefect.subItem: boolean columns: Windows writes the Access Yes/No true value (-1), iOS mixes 1 and -1
keptNotADefect.why: Not a Windows defect.

keptNotADefect.subItem: per-page selected area (BidPageSettings.BidAreaSelected) and inactive-area colouring
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: a deliberate Windows feature (areas are surfaced there, not on iOS).

keptNotADefect.subItem: iOS-only Connect, Tolerance, Snap-to-Linear controls (Windows has no UI for those columns)
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: the columns are part of the OST schema and Windows round-trips them untouched (its update writes only changed fields), it just has no UI for them.

keptNotADefect.subItem: area meshes: Windows inward (negative signed volume), iOS outward
keptNotADefect.why: Not a separate defect: inward in-memory winding of the area, linear and count generators is the Windows convention (the OBJ writer's face swap and the Python flip after the boolean are built around it).

keptNotADefect.subItem: flat quantized face shading on iOS instead of Windows' 60-degree crease-angle smooth shading
keptNotADefect.why: Not a Windows defect: crease-angle smooth shading is the intended Windows look; flat shading on iOS is a deliberate rendering-layer choice (PORTING_LOG 2026-03-23).

keptNotADefect.subItem: curved linear takeoffs: no curved placement and no centre handle on iOS
keptNotADefect.why: Not a Windows defect: Windows supports curved linears (arc band, three handles, 6-value position); iOS scope decision only.

keptNotADefect.subItem: camera refit on every empty-to-non-empty page selection on iOS; Windows keeps the camera within a bid
keptNotADefect.why: Not a Windows defect: the camera is fitted once per bid scene and kept across same-bid scene updates (pinned); the iOS transition refit is a deliberate iOS addition.

keptNotADefect.subItem: note 1: placement left running when the Image layer is hidden
keptNotADefect.why: Only an edge case: a condition assigned to the Image layer is hidden and unplaceable after the Image layer is hidden, while the placement tool stays armed (neither suspended nor restored).

keptNotADefect.subItem: whitespace-only Rise / Run: Windows rejects, old iOS accepted as 0
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: Windows rejects whitespace-only Rise and Run with 'Rise must be a number.' / 'Run must be a number.' (an empty field means 0).

keptNotADefect.subItem: 'Count as Negative Quantity' acts on the plan-view selected takeoffs only
keptNotADefect.why: Not a defect: Windows changes only the takeoffs passed in (the plan-view selection) and pushes one local history entry; this is the behaviour the iOS code change copies.

changedFiles.summary: Adds the 'Negative takeoff meshes' rule (new lines 502-516): one rule for the 3D view, HTML and OBJ/DXF/FBX (a negative subtracts only from positives of the same condition_type, a consumed positive is dropped, negatives never output, condition_type mandatory, writers use boolean results only, empty export returns False/None, drop-stub union failure keeps the wall and logs the takeoff uid). Every later AGENTS.md line shifts by +15 (MSH-14: 1456-1468 -> 1471-1483).

Two user-facing entries (new lines 13-21): OBJ and DXF (and FBX) cut like the 3D view and HTML export (same condition type only, fully removed takeoff left out, negative-only export fails like HTML); walls with a drop that cannot be joined stay visible and the log names the takeoff.

New _require_condition_types (lines 26-34), called first in apply_boolean_operations (line 42): any mesh whose metadata lacks 'condition_type' raises ValueError('Boolean operations need condition_type for takeoff <takeoff_uid>') before the native call, also for positive-only batches. Everything else unchanged: native call :56, flip loop :58-61, fallback to positives :63-71, boolean_union :74-85.

(a) export() returns False right after _apply_boolean_operations when processed_mesh_cache is empty, before _write_output (lines 78-79); (b) _apply_boolean_operations now puts condition.condition_type into every mesh metadata (line 163), so OBJ/DXF/FBX use the same-type rule as the 3D view and HTML; (c) new _exported_mesh_for_takeoff(takeoff) = processed_mesh_cache.get(takeoff.uid) (lines 214-215), i.e. writers never rebuild a mesh. Lines after 77 shift by +2, after 163 by +3 (EXP-06/11/12/21/22, MSH-16 citations).

Line 30: the DXF writer reads the post-boolean mesh through self._exported_mesh_for_takeoff(takeoff) instead of rebuilding with self._generate_mesh_for_takeoff(takeoff, condition). Line numbers of the file are unchanged.
Line 29: same change for the FBX writer (_exported_mesh_for_takeoff). FBX has no iOS counterpart (windows-only).

Line 76: the OBJ writer reads the post-boolean mesh through self._exported_mesh_for_takeoff(takeoff). A takeoff missing from processed_mesh_cache writes nothing but its condition keeps its '# name / g / usemtl' group header and MTL entry. Line numbers of the file are unchanged.

import logging and module logger (lines 1, 14); new static _union_with_drop_stub(takeoff, mesh, stub) (lines 94-111) used by the straight (line 91) and curved (line 161) wall branches: boolean_union that raises, returns None or returns a mesh without faces keeps the plain wall mesh and logs exactly one WARNING with the takeoff uid ('Drop stub union failed for takeoff <uid>; keeping the wall mesh', or '... raised ...' with exc_info when it raised); a good union is returned as is. Before, the factory returned None (takeoff dropped) or let the exception escape. All lines after 88 shift by +22 (MSH-08..11 citations).

New BooleanRuleContractTests (lines 69-100): test_mesh_without_condition_type_is_rejected_naming_the_takeoff (2 subtests) and test_typed_meshes_reach_the_native_rule; import of apply_boolean_operations (line 4).

Shared _ResultExporter._apply_boolean_operations double now leaves processed_mesh_cache['survivor'] (line 36), as a real export with a surviving positive does; new test_base_exporter_returns_false_without_writing_when_no_boolean_result_survives (lines 78-93). The other tests keep their assertions.

Imports the shared scenario (lines 1-18); test_writer_is_reset_and_receives_only_positive_feature_edges (23-62) now seeds processed_mesh_cache and makes _generate_mesh_for_takeoff raise AssertionError; new DXFExporterBooleanRuleTests (65-88), 4 tests through the real exporter and native booleans.
test_only_positive_generated_meshes_reach_writer_then_buffers_are_released seeds processed_mesh_cache (positive and negative) and asserts _generate_mesh_for_takeoff is never called (lines 26-28, 49).

Imports the shared scenario (9-19); test_export_resets_indices_skips_backouts_and_writes_paired_material_file (23-81) seeds the cache before each write and forbids rebuilds (the exact OBJ and MTL text is unchanged); new OBJExporterBooleanRuleTests (84-107), 4 tests.

New MeshFactoryDropStubUnionTests (lines 180-262): union returns None / raises / returns an empty mesh for a straight and a curved wall keeps the plain wall and logs one WARNING with the uid; a successful union is returned unchanged without a warning. rebaseline.notes: [Written 2026-11-16 while the Windows changes were uncommitted; Windows committed them as 6d4786f, see windowsBaseline.committedAs. The file names windows_uncommitted_v2.diff and windows_status_v2.txt were scratch files outside both repos.] Baseline check: the Windows git state is byte-identical to the saved v2 baseline (HEAD dceb47d, no new commits; git diff HEAD sha256 f5c0376d32bc37ee1f6e4914016372c123c558c9e539261cee3ad066c6c8e56d equals windows_uncommitted_v2.diff, git status --porcelain --ignored equals windows_status_v2.txt, boolean_rule_support.py sha256 16b774f8e929549c611db0de719bfb5df5b2641696ccd1abe7478e0fac774ee0 equals the baseline copy), so the current tree is the oracle. 18 paths changed: 2 docs (AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md), 6 production .py (boolean_operations, base_exporter, obj/dxf/fbx exporters, mesh_factory), 7 test files, 1 new untracked test helper, 2 qa json. No cpp_extensions file changed, the native rule (module_geometry.cpp) is untouched; all Windows tests pass. Decisions the Windows author made that close map questions: MSH-16 -> option (b) one rule for every format; EXP-22 -> option (b) one unified rule (negative-only fails, consumed positive dropped) but reported as a critical Export Error (WORKER_FAILED), not as a 'No Data' warning; MSH-19b -> option (b) keep the plain wall (the iOS behavior). The remaining open decisions from the old records are gone; only the winding sign (EXP-M02, GEO-15, EXP-13) is still a Windows inconsistency. iOS frame mapping for all new test inputs: Windows tests use an identity coordinate system (X = ost x, Y = ost y, Z up); the real Windows pipeline uses X = -x. iOS meshes are Y-up with (X, Z) = (-x_ost, -y_ost) (Core/Meshing/TakeoffMeshBuilder.hpp:8-9). A same-type cut that leaves ost x -10..0 therefore reads X 0..10 on iOS; the survivor at ost x 200 reads X -210..-190. Heights stay Y. Never assert the OBJ winding sign in boolean tests: the Windows sign depends on whether the export contains a negative mesh (EXP-M02: wall +57600 alone, -57600 with a cross-type negative present). iOS state on 2026-11-16 (before the fixes, superseded): Services/ExportService.mm and Services/ProjectService.mm used their own loops; since the final pass both call the shared Core boolean pass (Core/Meshing/BooleanPass.*, Core/Meshing/ExportMeshSet.*), so RB-01, RB-02, MSH-16, EXP-22, MSH-15 and EXP-05 are fixed, and MSH-19b and RB-04 are fixed in Core/Meshing/MeshFactory.cpp. The PARITY_MAP.md rows that cited the old behavior (feature-table rows of section G, the record texts of MSH-16, MSH-19b, EXP-22 and EXP-05) were updated with the 2026-11-16 decisions and rechecked in the 2026-11-18 final pass. FBX export (section H of PARITY_MAP.md: 'same boolean rule as OBJ/DXF') is windows-only and now also follows the same-type rule. open.title: note 1: Image-layer exemption on hide
open.text: Hiding the Image layer. WINDOWS ui_event_coordinator.py:6473-6476 skips _suspend_active_layer_tool when the hidden layer is the Image layer (and :6503-6504 skips the restore), so a placement of a condition on the Image layer keeps running on a condition that is hidden and unplaceable (a tap is ignored, placement_mode.py:1648). IOS: _suspendPlacementForLayerHide treats the Image layer like any other layer and leaves the placement tool. ASK: copy the exemption? (judged an edge case, not a Windows defect; low confidence)
open.iosMeanwhile: iOS leaves the placement tool when the Image layer of the placed condition is hidden (no exemption); the placement comes back on Show like for any other layer.
open.ask: Copy the Windows exemption (leave the tool running)? Windows behavior judged an edge case, not a defect.

open.title: note 2: layer-less conditions on Hide All
open.text: Hide All with an armed placement of a layer-less condition. WINDOWS ui_event_coordinator.py:1473-1489 never suspends the tool for a layer-less condition (pinned by a test) but project_data_service.py:664-678 marks every condition hidden on Hide All, so the tool stays armed on an unplaceable condition (possible Windows defect, consequence of LP-22). IOS: a layer-less condition is never suspended either (suspended_placement_for_layer_hide); Hide All writes only layer visibility and a layer-less condition stays visible and placeable (LP-22 stays wont-fix). ASK: nothing to port unless the Windows behavior is wanted byte for byte.
open.iosMeanwhile: A layer-less condition is never suspended (like Windows); Hide All writes only layer visibility, so a layer-less condition stays visible and placeable (LP-22 wont-fix).
open.ask: Nothing to port unless Windows behavior is wanted byte for byte (possible Windows defect, same root as LP-22).

items.title: iOS divides all mesh coordinates and dimensions by the page scale ratio; Windows meshes in raw OST units

windows.behavior: transform_to_3d(x,y) = (-(x/1.0), y/1.0) and ost_to_real_units(v) = v/1.0 for every page. The page sf2/sf1 never scales vertices, heights, thickness or offsets; it is only used for the page size in the flip/rotate transform. 3D coordinates are therefore OST (real-world) units for all pages.

ios.behavior: Every coordinate, height, thickness, width, depth and z offset is multiplied by 1/(sf2/sf1) of the takeoff's page. Model is paper-scale, different pages get different scales, and absolute tolerances (boolean kSnapTol 0.05, h_len < 0.001, arc radius tolerance 0.1, segment counts chord/5) act at a different relative size.

items.title: Takeoffs with a parent_uid are skipped for every condition type (attachments placed on areas count 0)

windows.behavior: primaries = takeoffs where (not condition.is_area) or parent_uid is root ('', '0', 'None'). Only AREA takeoffs with a parent are treated as holes. items.title: Fractional/mixed-number inches in condition-name elevations are not parsed; zero denominators and 1e20-scale values differ

windows.behavior: After the marker, the value text must pass is_elevation_text (prefix regexes in domain/services/elevation_text.py:3-33), then _parse_imperial_elevation searches: feet' [-] inches [n/d]" -> feet*12 + whole + n/d; bare inches-only forms 'whole n/d"' and 'n/d"' are accepted; fractions are float(n)/float(d); zero denominator raises ValueError('zero denominator in fraction n/d'); the MDB reader logs it and stores (0.0, False). Huge numerators/denominators stay finite floats.

ios.behavior: Reads one number then one unit char. The fraction branch after feet+whole inches is dead code (skip_spaces at :342 already consumed the space, so the 'name[i] == space' test at :350 never fires): "Slab @T 12' 6 1/2\"" -> 150 (Windows 150.5), "Wall @T 5' 6 11/16\"" -> 66 (66.6875). Inches-only mixed numbers and bare fractions ('6 1/2"', '1/2"', '11/16"') hit unit char '1' or '/' and return {0.0,false} (Windows 6.5, 0.5, 0.6875). Zero denominator never raises: "Slab @T 12' 6 1/0\"" -> (150, top) instead of (0.0,false). 'Wall @B 99999999999999999999/1"' -> 0 instead of 1e20.

items.title: ost_to_pdf_coordinates: iOS uses a stale legacy rotation/flip model; results differ for every rotation != 0

windows.behavior: points_per_unit=72*sf1/sf2. The point (x,y)*ppu in the UNROTATED page (top-left origin, width W, height H in pts) is flipped first (flip_x: W-x, flip_y: H-y), then rotated CCW: 90 gives (y, W-x), 180 gives (W-x, H-y), 270 gives (H-y, x). The result is returned with y' = output_height - y (Y-up PDF); output dims swap W/H for 90/270. Table for [10,20], W=600, H=800, sf1=1, sf2=2 (flips in order (none, flipY, flipX, both)): rot0 (360,80),(360,720),(240,80),(240,720); rot90 (720,360),(80,360),(720,240),(80,240); rot180 (240,720),(240,80),(360,720),(360,80); rot270 (80,240),(720,240),(80,360),(720,360).

ios.behavior: The legacy 14-argument function (coord_scale, is_page_rotated, auto_rotate_180, offsets) is retained. It applies flip against the rotated output size in OST units, then a reverse_rotation that is a reflection for 90/180/270. Same inputs: rot90 (-120,360),(720,360),(-120,440),(720,440); rot180 (240,80),(240,720),(360,80),(360,720); rot270 (720,440),(-120,440),(720,360),(-120,360). Rotation 0 matches Windows exactly (all four flip combos). PlanView passes coord_scale 1, flags false, offsets 0.

items.title: perp_slope() has the dx and dy tests swapped, breaking arc centers for axis-aligned chord segments

windows.behavior: perp_slope(dx,dy): dy==0 -> +inf; dx==0 -> 0.0; else -dx/dy. (1,0) -> inf, (0,1) -> 0.0, (0,0) -> inf.

ios.behavior: dx==0 -> +inf; dy==0 -> 0.0; else -dx/dy. (1,0) -> 0.0, (0,1) -> inf. A horizontal or vertical p1->control or control->p2 segment picks the wrong center formula, so arc length is wrong. Verified: position [1,0,0,1,1,1] curve=0 gives 1.6186 (Windows 2.1962, headline test expects pi/sqrt(2)=2.2214 +-0.03); arc (135,45,270 deg) R=100 gives 236.72 vs 392.64.

items.note: (test id for helper test is UomServiceTests... under LinearQuantity: class UomLinearQuantityTests::test_curve_helpers_agree_with_closed_forms). Fixing perp_slope alone is not enough: the direction (QTY-08) and at-end (QTY-09) rules must also change. Fixing perp_slope alone is not enough: QTY-08 and QTY-09 must change too. Core/Meshing/gen_curved.cpp has the same legacy arc rules (MSH-05, MSH-06, MSH-07).

items.title: Arc sweep direction uses the legacy cross-product rule instead of 'the arc through the control point'

windows.behavior: ccw_to_end = (end_angle-start_angle) mod 2pi; ccw_to_control = (control_angle-start_angle) mod 2pi; angle_diff = ccw_to_end if ccw_to_control <= ccw_to_end else ccw_to_end - 2pi. The arc always passes through the control point at any sweep. Owner-confirmed 2026-11-06 per the test docstring: start 0, control 250, end 251 deg at R=100 measures 438.1.

ios.behavior: clockwise = (cross1+cross2) < 0, then end_angle is shifted. This picks the minor arc when the control point is near one end of a >180 degree arc. items.title: Area slope: iOS applies a descending slope for opposite rise/run signs and uses the wrong rotation sense for its mirrored frame

windows.behavior: has_slope = run != 0 (rise/run truthy). proj = (x-cx)*cos(-rot)+(y-cy)*sin(-rot) in the Windows 3D frame (X=-x, Y=y). z_top = z_offset + thickness + span*prog*abs(rise)/abs(run), where prog=(proj-min)/span (span>0). The slope always rises along +proj. The sign of rise/run is ignored and only the takeoff rotation picks the direction (test: rise=-1 gives the same tops as rise=+1).

ios.behavior: asc = (rise>0&&run>0)||(rise<0&&run<0); if descending y = base + thickness + slope_h - h_chg. So rise=-1,run=4 gives a mirrored top, unlike Windows. proj uses rot=-rotation in the iOS (x,z)=(-x,-y) frame, i.e. X*cos(r)-Z*sin(r), whereas Windows is X*cos(r)+Z*sin(r) after Z=-Y. items.title: Metric elevations: compound m+cm without 'and'/'+' dropped, '+' glued form fails, decimal comma, 'centimeters', signs, word boundaries

windows.behavior: Accepted shapes: '[-]N[.|,]N m [and|+] [-]N[.|,]N cm' (the connector is OPTIONAL), 'N m|meter|meters', 'N cm|centimeter|centimeters', case-insensitive, decimal comma = point, unit must end at a word boundary ('5cmx' invalid). A leading minus on the metres part negates metres+cm together; a minus on cm alone subtracts. Result cm/2.54 inches.

ios.behavior: Number scanner accepts digits and '.' only (no comma). Only the first number is used unless the text after the unit starts with 'and' or '+' separated by a space: "Wall @T 1m 20cm" -> 100 cm only (39.37 in; Windows 47.244 in), "1.5m 20cm" -> 150 cm, "3m+20cm" -> 0 (rest_low[1]=='+' fails the 'm' test at :384), "2,5 m" -> 0, "2 CENTIMETERS"/"2 centimeter" -> 0 (only prefix 'cm' recognised), "-1m 20cm" -> -100 cm, "1m -20cm" -> 100 cm. Accepts glued tails ('5cmx' -> 1.97 in, '12 cmx') that Windows rejects.

items.statusNote: Metric grammar ported (optional and/+ connector, glued +, decimal comma, centimeter(s)/meter(s), case-insensitive, word boundary after the unit, sign of metres applies to metres+cm, minus on cm subtracts). Product and sum are separate statements so an FMA-contracting compiler cannot change the IEEE rounding.

items.title: Elevation marker detection differs (first '@' vs last ' @T'/' @B' / ' @ ' / ' @'; leading space; case)

windows.behavior: Marker must be preceded by a space; the LAST ' @T' or ' @B' wins; if none, the last ' @ ' or ' @' is a legacy bare marker (bottom). T/B are case-sensitive: ' @t' falls to the bare-marker rule and its value 't 5...' is not an elevation. Text with '@' not preceded by a space ('Wall@T 5' 0"', '@T 6"', 'a@b @T ...') is not a marker.

ios.behavior: Uses name.find('@') (FIRST '@' anywhere), then optionally eats a 't'/'T'/'b'/'B', case-insensitive. 'Wall @T 5' 6" @B 3' 0"' -> (66, top) (Windows (36, bottom)); 'Wall@T 5' 0"' -> (60, top) (Windows none); '@T 6"' -> (6, top) (Windows none); 'Wall @t 5' 0"' -> (60, top) (Windows none); 'Wall email@x.com @T 5' 0"' -> (0,false) because the first '@' is in the e-mail (Windows (60, top)).

items.testPlan: extract_z_value on: "Wall @T 5' 6\" @B 3' 0\"" -> (36.0,false); "Wall @B 3' 0\" @T 5' 6\"" -> (66.0,true); "A @T 1/2\" @T 3/4\"" -> (0.75,true); "Wall @ 6\"" -> (6.0,false) (legacy bare marker = bottom); "Wall @ 6 1/2\"" -> (6.5,false); " @T 6\"" -> (6.0,true) (empty base name); "@T 6\"" -> (0,false); "Wall@T 5' 0\"" -> (0,false); "Wall @t 5' 0\"" -> (0,false); "Wall email@x.com @T 5' 0\"" -> (60.0,true) (last two verified by running the Windows code, not in its tests).

items.title: inches_to_display rounds half away from zero; Windows round() is banker's rounding; non-finite input not handled

windows.behavior: eighths = round(abs(inches)*8) with Python round-half-to-even; non-finite input returns ''. 0.0625 -> '' ; 0.3125 -> '1/4"'; 0.5625 -> '1/2"'; 0.8125 -> '3/4"'; 1.0625 -> '1"'; 1.3125 -> '1 1/4"'; 12.0625 -> '1' 0"'; 24.5625 -> '2' 0 1/2"'. Exactly 1/16-odd multiples (a common drawing dimension, e.g. 5/16") hit the tie.

ios.behavior: C round(): 0.0625 -> '1/8"', 0.3125 -> '3/8"', 0.5625 -> '5/8"', 0.8125 -> '7/8"', 1.0625 -> '1 1/8"'. NaN/inf cast to int is undefined behaviour. 288 of the 576 +/-k/16 values up to 3 ft differ (checked with a Python replica of the iOS arithmetic). Because the edit dialog re-parses the displayed text on save, the rounded value is also what gets persisted.

items.note: The Windows tests never test an odd-sixteenth tie, so the banker's behaviour is unpinned but it is what the Windows code does now. Flagged 'fix' because behaviour is clear and reproducible; if the product owner considers the Windows tie result a bug, this becomes needs-decision. Use std::nearbyint under FE_TONEAREST (ties to even), not round().

items.title: No UID remapping: PK collisions overwrite other projects' rows (INSERT OR REPLACE); original UIDs kept; no global UID floor

windows.behavior: Every imported row gets a fresh UID. The floor is the max of MAX(UID) over Bids, CdnTypes, JobStatuses, all BID_SECTIONS tables (incl. BidEmployees), BidPages, BidNamedViews, BidHotLinks and all PAGE_SECTIONS tables, and of every child FK column that references those UIDs (BID_RELATIONSHIPS). New CdnTypes then JobStatuses rows take floor+1, +2, ...; the graph continues from the last one. _build_uid_map assigns next uids in this order: bid row, bid_tables in order [BID_SECTIONS..., BidPages, BidNamedViews, BidHotLinks], each row in file order, then page_tables in first-seen key order. Rows with UID '', missing or '0' get none, and a repeated UID shares one new UID. FK fields in the bid-internal set (UID, BidUID, BidPageUID, BidConditionUID, BidLayerUID, BidZoneUID, BidAreaUID, BidTypAreaUID, ParentUID, ParentCommentUID, MasterPageUID, MasterAreaUID, TranslateAreaUID, BidConditionFolderUID, BidPageFolderUID, BidTakeoffFromUID, BidTakeoffToUID, BidPageViewUID, TypGroupTakeoffUID, TypPageTakeoffUID, TypGroupMarkerUID, TypGroupUID) map through that table, with unknown values left unchanged. BidPageSelectedUID maps through the page map only, otherwise NULL. CdnTypeUID is mapped through the master map (unmapped kept). The original file is never mutated. The exporter writes several tables in descending UID order, so ascending new UIDs reverse stored row order for those tables.

The same happens for template BidLayers seeded at UIDs 1-4. A file with duplicate UIDs inside one table silently keeps the last row. If the Bid has no UID attribute, SQLite auto-assigns a Bids.UID while children keep BidUID values that point nowhere.

items.title: CAB reader silently skips corrupt blocks, ignores checksums and treats PDF extraction failure as success

windows.behavior: FDICopy extracts through the Windows cabinet library. Any decode or corruption error makes extract_cab return false, the import fails with 'the OSP archive could not be extracted', and nothing is imported. The legacy test fixtures write CFDATA checksum 0 (meaning none).

ios.where: Core/Import/CabExtractor.cpp:176-258 (blocks with missing 'CK' or an inflate error are skipped with continue; csum at offset 0 never read); Services/ImportService.mm:203-216
ios.behavior: A bad MSZIP block is dropped without error, so every later byte in that folder shifts. extract_cab_file only fails if the resulting buffer is shorter than the file's end; otherwise it returns shifted, wrong bytes. There is no check that produced bytes equal cbUncomp. CFDATA checksums are not verified. Stored-block truncation just breaks the loop. Failed or empty PDF extraction is ignored and the import proceeds.

items.testPlan: Build a two-block MSZIP CAB (raw deflate with 'CK' prefix, block 2 using block 1 as dictionary) containing an OST then a PDF; assert both extract byte-identically. Then corrupt block 1's deflate bytes (and separately flip one byte of a CFDATA payload with non-zero csum): extract must fail (empty result and the import must report an extraction error), never return shifted bytes. A PDF whose extraction fails must fail the OSP import. A stored (uncompressed) CAB with csum 0, as in _write_legacy_ansi_cab, must still extract.
items.note: Windows FDI behavior on bad checksums is the documented library behavior (I could not run FDI here). The 'fail on corruption' rule is clear from the Windows tests (extract_cab false means the import fails). A host test needs a zlib on the build machine.
items.statusNote: importOSPFile no longer extracts per member and ignores failures: stage_osp_package uses the single streaming extraction, so any corrupt block / checksum / short member fails the import ('The OSP archive could not be extracted') before anything is staged or imported.

items.title: CdnTypes/JobStatuses reconciliation differs (key normalisation, ambiguity errors, UID allocation, unmapped refs)

windows.behavior: Identity key for CdnTypes.Name is text.strip().lower(); JobStatuses.Name is exact text. Incoming rows that collapse to the same key raise AmbiguousMasterDataIdentityError, and so do existing DB rows that share a key (the import is rolled back). An existing match maps old UID to the existing UID; otherwise a new UID = running floor+1 is inserted. Remap: JobStatusUID not in the map, or '0', becomes NULL; CdnTypeUID not in the map is left as is and '0' becomes NULL.

possibleWindowsDefect.what: boolean_operations.py flips every mesh the native call returns, but the native code returns meshes with two different windings: meshes that went through the boolean come out normalised (outward) and the Python flip turns them into the generators' inward convention (the OBJ writer's face swap then makes them outward in the file), whereas positives that have no same-type negative in the export are returned untouched (already inward) and the same flip turns them outward (the OBJ swap then makes them inward). So one OBJ mixes both windings, and adding a negative anywhere in the export turns every untouched positive of another type inside-out.
possibleWindowsDefect.scenario: A bid with a wall condition and, on another condition type, a negative area: the exported OBJ shows the wall's faces inward and the cut slab outward. Viewers that cull back faces (and slicers that read the signed volume) show or treat the wall as inside-out; removing the negative flips the wall back.
possibleWindowsDefect.subItem: OBJ winding of untouched positives flips as soon as the export holds a negative
possibleWindowsDefect.evidence: Re-executed the real MeshGenerator, apply_boolean_operations (native ost_geometry.pyd) and OBJMeshWriter._transform_faces (signed volume as written to the OBJ). No negative in the export: wall +48000 and slab +40000 (all outward). Cross-type area negative: untouched wall -48000 (inward) next to the cut slab +36400 (outward). Same-type cut wall +46568.9. Extra control run: a same-type negative far away (disjoint boxes) leaves both walls at +48000, so the inversion needs a negative of ANOTHER type. The only Windows test of the flip mocks boolean_union and never covers a passthrough positive; test_mesh.py:234-241 says the sign is deliberately not asserted.
possibleWindowsDefect.suggestedWindowsFix: Flip only meshes that Manifold produced: the native apply_boolean_operations already marks them (metadata boolean_applied at module_geometry.cpp:90); make boolean_operations.py:59 flip only entries with that flag, or normalise winding once (for example by signed volume) after the pass. windows.behavior:
Groups are keyed by condition_uid in first-seen order over [non-area takeoffs..., area parent takeoffs...]. Material and layer name = sanitize('{cdn_type_name or Unknown}_{condition.name or Condition_<uid>}_{uid[:8]}'). OBJ per group: '# <original name>', 'g <mat>', 'usemtl <mat>', all that condition's positive meshes (continuous 1-based indices), then a blank line. MTL has one newmtl per condition. Conditions that have only negative takeoffs still get an empty OBJ group, an MTL entry and a DXF layer. DXF layers are created for every condition in the exportable set, and LINEs are tagged with that layer. [Rebaselined 2026-11-16] Unchanged for exports without negatives. New: groups/materials/layers are built from takeoffs_by_group (every exportable condition), the meshes only from the boolean result, so an empty group stays. Verified (identity coordinate system) for consumed = [consumed(count,0), survivor(count,200), negative(count_block,0)]: OBJ text '# Created by OST Visualizer
mtllib model.mtl

# count
g Unknown_count_count
usemtl Unknown_count_count
' + 8 'v' lines (x 190/210, y 0/10, z +-10) + 12 'f' lines + '
# count_block
g Unknown_count_block_count_bl
usemtl Unknown_count_block_count_bl

'; MTL header '# Display Mode: Solid', '# Materials: 2' with newmtl Unknown_count_count and newmtl Unknown_count_block_count_bl; the DXF has layers for both (12 LINEs, all on the count layer). other_type = [positive(count,0), negative(attachment,10)]: OBJ groups '# count' (8 v, 12 f) then an empty '# attachment' group, MTL Materials: 2.

ios.behavior: OBJ: one group and one material per positive mesh named sanitize(condition.name+'_'+index), in project.takeoffs order, with no '# name' comment and no empty groups. DXF: layer name = raw condition.name (unsanitised, 'Layer_<i>' if empty). Conditions with the same name merge into one layer (add_layer overwrites the colour; last colour wins). Only meshes that were produced get a layer. HTML: names are '<name>_<i>'.

items.title: Polygon close detection uses the snapped tap point and a strict canvas distance; Windows uses the raw cursor and <= 12 viewport px

windows.behavior: If len(points) >= 3 and the raw cursor viewport position is within 12 px (<=) of the first point, the polygon closes (if valid) without appending a point.

ios.behavior: Computes the tap OST after grid rounding and angle snapping from the last point, converts that back to canvas and tests distance < 12/zoom, so angle snapping can pull the point more than 12 pt away from the first point and prevent closing.

The boundary distance is inclusive (12 px closes).
items.note: Closing an invalid polygon neither flashes nor appends, on both sides.
items.statusNote: Core ost_placement::polygon_close_hit (>= 3 points and raw cursor <= 12 px, inclusive). PlanView _handlePlaceTap measures the RAW tap against the first point in screen points (canvas distance * zoomScale) before any snapping; an invalid polygon neither closes nor appends. The strict canvas-distance test on the snapped point is removed.

items.title: Count shapes: hexagon, octagon, rhombus orientation and size, and ellipse rotation differ

windows.behavior: Ellipse/circle: a 32-gon with radii (w/2, d/2) rotated by the takeoff rotation. Triangle: apex (0,-d/2), base (+-w/2, +d/2). Rhombus: points (0,-w/2),(0.575*w/2,0),(0,w/2),(-0.575*w/2,0) using width only. Hexagon: 6 vertices from angle 0 at radius w/2 on both axes; octagon: 8 vertices from angle pi/8 at radius w/2 (depth ignored). All rotated by rotation (radians).

ios.behavior: Analytic ellipse with rotation ignored; rhombus uses ry (depth) vertically; hexagon and octagon via regularPolygonPoints(cx,cy,rx,ry,n) starting at -90 degrees with ry radius. Triangle, rectangle and square match.

items.title: OSP image reference resolution and path rewrite rules differ

windows.behavior: Only BidPage elements (anywhere under the root) and only ImagePath/OverlayImagePath values with extension .pdf/.tif/.tiff are considered. A value starting with TempImages!.tmp is looked up exactly (case-insensitive); any other value matches the packaged member with the deepest path-suffix match (flat member 'a.pdf' matches only if reference ends in it; nested member requires all its parts as suffix; no basename fallback into nested members). Unresolved references are logged as one warning ('OSP import could not resolve N referenced image(s) ...') and their original value is kept untouched. Only references that resolved are rewritten, and the OST is re-serialised only if something changed. Each attribute is checked independently.

ios.behavior: Every .pdf entry anywhere is extracted by basename and every non-empty ImagePath/OverlayImagePath of every child of BidPages is rewritten to <dest>/<basename of the original value> regardless of extension, of whether the file exists, or of whether it was in the package. Missing images lose their original path (pointing at a non-existent file); .tif/.tiff are never extracted but still rewritten; resolution is by basename only, so a nested reference and a flat one with the same basename cannot be told apart. The element tag is not checked (any child of BidPages).

windows.behavior: The first point of a linear or rectangle and the drag origin are the exact press position.

items.title: Area tessellation: earcut is fed a mirrored frame, so the triangle set and diagonals differ from Windows

windows.behavior: The 2D ring handed to earcut is the 3D (X,Y) = (-x, +y) footprint of the bottom vertices (holes appended with hole start indices). Bottom triangles use the earcut order as-is; the top ring is reversed. Verified faces for the square [0,0,4,0,4,4,0,4] thickness 1: bottom (1,0,3),(3,2,1); top (7,4,5),(5,6,7).

ios.behavior: polygon is built from vertices in the iOS (x,z) = (-x,-y) frame, which is the Windows frame mirrored in Y. Earcut ear selection and diagonals depend on orientation, so the same polygon gets different triangles: bottom (2,3,0),(0,1,2) (the other diagonal) for the square; holes and L-shapes also differ. Verified on 7 cases (square CW/CCW, L-shape, three hole configurations, two holes): triangle sets differ even ignoring winding. Feeding earcut {x,-z} (the Windows frame) gives identical triangle sets in all 7 cases (patched copy in the harness).

Cases for the same comparison: CW square, L-shape [0,0,4,0,4,1,1,1,1,3,0,3], hole CW in CCW, hole CW in CW, two holes in a 10x10.
items.note: Vertex arrays are already identical under the (X,Y,Z)->(X,Z,-Y) mapping, so only the earcut input frame and the winding (GEO-15) differ. Geometry (area, volume) is the same; this only affects face lists and ordering in exports and boolean tie-breaks. Overlaps with the meshing mapper.

windows.behavior: Measured on real Windows HTML scenes: signed volume of wall -57600, column -13824, circle -21467.487, slab -57600, and mean(outward . normal) is negative for all of them, so normals point inward. When the export contains any negative takeoff, apply_boolean_operations flips every returned positive, including ones untouched because the negative has another condition type: that slab came out +60000 (outward). The Windows shader computes diffuse as max(dot(normal, lightDir), 0) from the raw normal attribute, so the normal sign changes the lighting. [Rebaselined 2026-11-16] Unchanged for HTML. Measured for OBJ with the real OSTCoordinateSystem (default page): wall [0,0,100,0] height 96 thickness 6 -> OBJ signed volume +57600 with no negative in the export, -57600 when the export also holds a negative takeoff of another condition type (a far-away negative slab) although the wall is untouched; slab [0,0,100,0,100,100,0,100] thickness 6 z 0: +60000 alone, -60000 next to a cross-type negative; a same-type cut piece comes out outward (+54144 for the wall with a crossing same-type negative). With the identity test coordinate system the same effect shows as +4000 / -4000 for the 20x20x10 count box (OBJ). So untouched positives flip orientation as soon as any negative mesh exists, cut pieces do not: Windows is inconsistent within one file. The new Windows tests only read x spans, never the winding.

ios.behavior: Normals are area-weighted sums of the iOS face winding: boxes are outward (positive volume), cylinders and curved walls inward (EXP-13). The iOS Phong flatShading material does not use the attribute, so there is no visible effect today.

possibleWindowsDefect.what: Same root cause as EXP-13, seen through the HTML export. The lighting normals are derived from the face winding (only +z is forced) and the viewer lights with the raw normal and no flip. Because the boolean wrapper flips untouched positives only when the export holds a negative of another type, the side-face normals of the same wall change sign depending on whether such a negative exists, so its lighting changes. Using inward-winding meshes with a raw-normal shader that matches the native renderer is a design choice; the data-dependent sign is the defect.
possibleWindowsDefect.scenario: Export one wall to HTML: its vertical faces are lit from the inward-normal side. Add a negative area of another condition type anywhere in the selection and export again: the same wall's vertical faces are lit from the opposite side.

The HTML path calls the same apply_boolean_operations. The shader was not run; the conclusion rests on the normal buffer and viewer.html's nativeLitColor source.
possibleWindowsDefect.suggestedWindowsFix: Same as EXP-13: flip only meshes that Manifold produced (flag boolean_applied) so winding, and therefore the shading normal, does not depend on whether any negative exists.

items.title: CAB member names are not decoded (legacy ANSI code page vs UTF-8 flag)

windows.behavior: Names are decoded as UTF-8 when the CFFILE attribute _A_NAME_IS_UTF (0x80) is set, otherwise with the system ANSI code page (CP_ACP) and re-encoded as UTF-8. Decode failure aborts the listing/extraction.

ios.behavior: Name bytes are used as is (backslash converted to slash), and the attribute flag is ignored. A legacy ANSI name containing a byte like 0x96 (en dash in cp1252) is invalid UTF-8, so [NSString stringWithUTF8String:] on the destination dir/file path returns nil. The directory/PDF writes would then fail or throw and the rewritten ImagePath would hold invalid UTF-8. Could not be run on a device.

items.note: CP_ACP is machine-dependent on Windows (the tests assume cp1252). The decision is which fixed code page iOS should assume for non-UTF-flagged names; cp1252 matches the Windows fixtures. Verifier: Windows decode_cab_member (cab_compressor.cpp:83-89) uses UTF-8 when attribs&0x80 and otherwise CP_ACP, which depends on the machine (tests assume cp1252). iOS ignores the flag and uses raw bytes, so a legacy ANSI name like the Windows fixture '26-061 412 - Corporate Lot K, KS.ost' (cp1252 0x96) is invalid UTF-8 and the NSString built from dest_dir becomes nil (ImportService.mm:184-185,206-215; not runnable here). The divergence is real and plausible in real legacy OSPs; the fixed code page to assume (cp1252) is the decision.

items.title: DATETIME and binary column values stored as raw text

windows.behavior: DATETIME columns (14, e.g. Bids.CreateDateTime, ModDateTime, BidDate, CopyTimeStamp): a value with exactly 6 whitespace-separated integers 'Y M D h m s' becomes a datetime; anything else (blank, ISO, 3 parts, month 13, non-numeric) becomes NULL. Memo/IMAGE columns (30, e.g. Bids.Notes, BidTakeoffs.Position, BidTexts.Name): '' becomes NULL, text becomes UTF-8 bytes, and BidTexts/BidCallOuts.Name become latin-1 bytes.

ios.behavior: Everything is stored as TEXT, so '2026 7 19 0 39 2' stays that string and invalid dates are kept instead of NULL. Binary columns hold UTF-8 text. Load reads bid_date/copy_timestamp as strings, and Settings.Created is written by create_schema as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', so the DB mixes two date formats.

items.testPlan: If a datetime representation is chosen: '2024 3 9 14 5 7' maps to a valid date; '', '2024-03-09', '2024 3 9', '2024 13 9 1 1 1' and 'a b c d e f' map to NULL.

items.statusNote: The decided DATETIME rule itself (raw 6-part string, NULL when invalid) and the memo text rule are fixed and tested (Imp20_* in test_import_column_types.cpp). DECIDED 2026-11-19 (keep iOS, no code change, all three sub-rules): (1) a DATETIME integer outside the C int range stores NULL and the import goes on (Windows import_operations.py:594-610 fails the whole import with OverflowError; possible Windows defect, low confidence); (2) BidTexts.Name and BidCallOuts.Name are stored as UTF-8 text (Windows import_operations.py:613-615 + serialization.py:7-8,70-73 store latin-1 bytes; not a defect on the import side, but the same latin-1 rule also rejects non-latin-1 annotation text inside Windows, annotation_operations.py:255-257: possible Windows defect); (3) memo and IMAGE text columns stay TEXT (Windows import_operations.py:616 stores a UTF-8 BLOB; not a defect). The numeric analogue IMP-05 (an integer above 64 bits fails like Windows) is unchanged.

openQuestions.text: Three sub-behaviours of the DATETIME / binary column rule are not the plain Windows behaviour (the decided date rule "raw 6-part string, NULL when invalid" itself is done). (1) WINDOWS ost_visualizer/infrastructure/mdb/components/import_operations.py:597-609 catches only (ValueError, TypeError): a DATETIME integer outside the C int range (e.g. "99999999999 1 1 0 0 0") raises OverflowError and the whole import fails and rolls back (see tests/infrastructure/mdb/components/test_import_operations.py:3079 test_an_absurd_datetime_text_raises_overflow_characterisation, "characterisation, not a requirement"); IOS stores NULL and the import goes on. The numeric analogue IMP-05 (an integer of more than 64 bits fails with "Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER") still fails like Windows: decide it together. (2) WINDOWS import_operations.py:613-615 + serialization.py:7-8,70-73 encode_annotation_text stores BidTexts.Name / BidCallOuts.Name as latin-1 bytes (raises for any character outside latin-1, e.g. euro sign U+20AC); unsafe on iOS (not valid UTF-8, OstDatabase.cpp:162 reads UTF-8, nil NSString risk); IOS stores UTF-8 TEXT (iOS never reads those columns). (3) WINDOWS import_operations.py:616 encode_text_blob stores memo/IMAGE text as a BLOB; IOS keeps TEXT (the writers bind_text, OstDatabase has no bind_blob, ProjectStore+Takeoffs.cpp:542-545 does not capture BLOB columns). (2) BidTexts.Name and BidCallOuts.Name are stored as UTF-8 text (Windows: latin-1 bytes, raising for characters outside latin-1). No code change. (3) Memo and IMAGE (longbinary) text columns stay TEXT (Windows: UTF-8 BLOB). No code change. The decision of 2026-11-16 (option a) is applied.

possibleWindowsDefect.what: Bad date texts are handled in two ways: out-of-range values such as year 10000 or month 13 raise ValueError and read as NULL, while an integer beyond the C long range raises OverflowError, which is not caught, so one corrupt date aborts the entire import. It fails closed (rolled back, returns False), only a hand-made or corrupt file reaches it, and the Windows test itself calls it a characterisation with an open owner question (while the class docstring says overflow is meant to propagate), so intent is unclear. The threshold is also platform dependent (C long is 32-bit on Windows, 64-bit elsewhere).
possibleWindowsDefect.scenario: An .ost whose DATETIME field holds '2147483648 1 1 0 0 0': the whole bid import is rolled back with a generic failure, while '10000 1 1 0 0 0' in the same place imports with a NULL date.
possibleWindowsDefect.subItem: (1) DATETIME integer outside the C long range raises OverflowError and fails the whole import (iOS stores NULL)
possibleWindowsDefect.evidence: Re-executed the real _convert_access_value: '10000 1 1 0 0 0' -> None, '2024 13 9 1 1 1' -> None, '99999999999 1 1 0 0 0' and '2147483648 1 1 0 0 0' -> OverflowError. Windows' own exporter only writes in-range dates, so a Windows round trip never hits it.
possibleWindowsDefect.suggestedWindowsFix: Change line 608 to `except (ValueError, TypeError, OverflowError)` and flip the characterisation test (test_import_operations.py:3079) to expect None, if NULL like the other bad dates is wanted; otherwise document the fail-closed rule in the class docstring.
whereNotes: tests/infrastructure/mdb/components/test_import_operations.py:3079-3084 (characterisation test with an open owner question)

furtherPossibleWindowsDefects.what: Beyond the import: the Windows text and callout annotation write path uses the same latin-1 encoder and no latin-1 guard exists in the UI (grep for latin-1 / cp1252 in ost_visualizer finds only serialization.py and parsers/utils/parser.py). Common pasted characters (euro sign, curly quotes, em dash, CJK) therefore fail at save time, and the warning that appears blames Page and Layer settings, not the text. Nothing is corrupted (fail-closed) and the refusal itself is test-pinned, so this is a usability inconsistency, not data loss. The full UI placement path was not traced end to end.
furtherPossibleWindowsDefects.scenario: A Windows user pastes a text with a euro sign or curly quotes into a Text annotation: the annotation is not saved and the message points at Page and Layer settings.
furtherPossibleWindowsDefects.subItem: (2b) same latin-1 rule inside the Windows app: text/callout annotations with characters outside latin-1 cannot be saved
furtherPossibleWindowsDefects.evidence: Re-executed the real AnnotationOperationsMixin._text_annotation_name_value: 'Price <euro>5' and 'say <curly quotes>hi<curly quotes>' raise UnicodeEncodeError. insert_annotations catches the exception, logs 'Failed to bulk insert annotations' and returns []; the plan-view handler then shows the generic Page/Layer warning. grep of presentation/application/domain for isascii/encode guards on annotation text: none.
furtherPossibleWindowsDefects.suggestedWindowsFix: Validate the text against latin-1 in the annotation editor with a specific message, or, if the legacy OST reader really is Windows-1252, encode with cp1252 (covers euro and curly quotes) and keep the error only for the rest.

ios.behavior: extract_cab_file calls decompress_folder, which inflates the whole folder into a std::vector, and importOSPFile calls it once per PDF plus once for the OST. windows.behavior: One rule on every path. (1) A negative subtracts only from positives whose condition_type equals the negative's condition_type (native negatives_by_type, module_geometry.cpp:25,76-79; native code unchanged). (2) A positive that same-type negatives remove completely is dropped: module_geometry.cpp:80-93 has no else, so the result list has no entry for it. (3) Negatives are never output. (4) Positives with no negative of their type come out unchanged (module_geometry.cpp:95-103). (5) condition_type is mandatory (boolean_operations.py:26-34,42 raises ValueError, see RB-01). OBJ/DXF/FBX take condition_type from the condition (base_exporter.py:163) and write only meshes found in processed_mesh_cache (base_exporter.py:214-215; obj_exporter.py:76, dxf_exporter.py:30, fbx_exporter.py:29): a consumed positive is skipped and never regenerated. Verified numerically with apply_boolean_operations on unit boxes: positive box (0,0,0)-(10,10,10) type 1 + negative box x 5..15 type 0 -> positive unchanged (8 vertices, 12 faces, |vol| 1000); same with negative type 1 -> 8 vertices, 12 faces, |vol| 500; same-type negative box (-5,-5,-5)-(15,15,15) -> no meshes; cross-type covering negative -> positive unchanged (|vol| 1000); negative only -> no meshes.

items.title: Parent token 'None' counts as a root takeoff in Windows quantities but as a hole in iOS (Windows is internally inconsistent)

windows.behavior: compute_page_quantities treats parent_uid in ('', '0', 'None') as root, but Takeoff.is_hole (and the loader contract checks) treat only '' and '0' as root, so 'None' is a hole elsewhere. Quantity tests pin the 'None' = root behavior.

ios.behavior: is_hole() = non-empty and != '0', so a takeoff with parent 'None' is skipped as a hole and its quantity is lost; 'None' parents also become hole owners. Verified: Windows 198 vs iOS 197 for backout test; sentinel test Windows 212 vs iOS 204.

Possible Windows defect for (b): takeoff_renderer.py:105-116 and :390-417 + zoom_handler.py:339-348, :362-379 draw the marker displaced from its shape on a rotated or flipped page. items.title: DXF LINE entity order is the std::unordered_set iteration order of the STL in use

windows.behavior: Edges come from an unordered_set in MSVC STL iteration order, so the LINE order in the DXF is MSVC-specific.

ios.behavior: The same algorithm on libc++, whose unordered_set iteration order differs. LINE order (and which endpoint is first in a LINE) can differ from Windows.

items.testPlan: Compare DXF files as sets of unordered endpoint pairs per layer (as done in the mapping run), not as byte streams; byte-equality of the whole DXF cannot be required across STLs.
items.note: CAD semantics are order-independent. The DXFWriter itself is byte-identical for the same line list. Verifier: LINE entity order follows unordered_set iteration (feature_edges.cpp:109-175), which is MSVC STL specific and cannot be matched under libc++. Correction to the mapper's note: UndirectedEdge is normalised to (min,max), so which endpoint comes first in a LINE depends only on mesh vertex order, not on the STL; it differs today only because of EXP-17. Compare as unordered sets, which I did (equal after the EXP-02 mapping).
items.statusNote: Not reproducible on iOS: DXF entity order is the iteration order of std::unordered_set of the STL in use (open disposition, nothing to port).

A value whose faces are all degenerate (or that has no faces) is not treated as a failure: make_result still says valid (vertices remain), TakeoffMeshBuilder.cpp:233 then drops the whole takeoff and the old ExportService/ProjectService loops would pass a vertex-only mesh on, so the wall disappears or is empty where Windows keeps the plain wall. An exception other than std::exception would escape. No warning is logged (Core has no log facility).

items.testPlan: Reuse the Windows inputs of MeshFactoryDropStubUnionTests: Linear condition height 10, thickness 2, drop_run true, drop_value 4.0; takeoffs [0,0,100,0] and curved [0,0,100,0,50,20] curve 0 (iOS call with scale 1.0). Make boolean_union controllable in the host tests (extend Config/Tests/Support/BooleanOpsStub.cpp with a test-set behavior: nullopt, empty CppMeshData, CppMeshData with vertices but zero faces, a fixed 3-vertex/1-face mesh) and expect: for nullopt, empty and zero-face results the result equals the plain wall (same vertices and faces as the same takeoff with drop_run false; Windows plain wall: straight 8 vertices / 12 faces, curved 100 / 196, counts differ on iOS only by EXP-17/MSH-05) and valid == true; for the fixed good mesh that mesh is returned unchanged. Expose the failure to the caller (for example a MeshResult flag drop_stub_union_failed) so the ObjC layer can NSLog 'Drop stub union failed for takeoff <uid>; keeping the wall mesh'; test the flag, not the log text. Wrap the union call in try/catch(...) and treat a throw as failure (Windows 'raises' case).
